In accordance with Agreement Between Owner and Design-Builder (Contract) dated 10/7/2024 and fully executed on 10/9/2024, Article 3, Para GC-3.9.3 Notice of Delay, Korsmo Construction is notifying Bremerton School District of time impacts due to delays for the View Ridge Elementary Arts Academy Replacement. This Notice is directly associated with the Building Permit Review and Issuance Delays from the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ), the City of Bremerton. As substantiated within the attached “251218 BSD Notice of Delay and Potential Impacts”, the scheduled date for issuance of the City of Bremerton Building Permit for View Ridge Elementary Arts Academy Replacement (VREAA) Monday 11/10/2025. Following initial delay of permit issuance, Korsmo Construction, TCF Architecture, Consertus, and the City of Bremerton Fire Marshall met in a weekly cadence a dozen times, to coordinate expectations and status updates. During Foundation-Only Permit Preconstruction Meeting with the City of Bremerton Building Inspectors on 12/10/25, the project team was notified that no vertical construction would be allowed prior to Building Permit Issuance. Korsmo Construction received the City of Bremerton Building Permit on 2/24/26. This notice is issued within seven (7) days of the event causing delay, namely the extended review and delayed issuance of the City of Bremerton Building Permit, which directly prevented commencement of vertical construction activities. Based on preliminary evaluation, the permit delay has impacted the project’s Critical Path activities associated with structural foundation work and vertical construction sequencing. The full duration and extent of schedule impact will be demonstrated through an updated CPM schedule analysis currently in development. Korsmo Construction has undertaken reasonable mitigation efforts, including resequencing work, recurring coordination meetings with the City of Bremerton, the Design Team, and Owner’s representatives, and will continue to pursue all commercially reasonable measures to mitigate further impacts. Pursuant to contract language GC-4.1.6, Korsmo is issuing this formal notice of Claim for Additional Time. Upon evaluation and quantification of the actual project delay, Korsmo will issue a revised CPM schedule indicating extent of time impacts. Further, Korsmo will work with the project contractors to investigate mitigation efforts possible to improve associated impacts. We remain confident that we can resolve all issues in a cooperative manner and will continue to work with the best interests of the Bremerton School District to complete these project scopes as diligently and expeditiously as possible. In doing so, Korsmo waives no provisions of the contract and explicitly reserves its right to assert claim/notice provisions. Box 11124 — Fort Smith, Arkansas 72917 Phone (479) 709-0044 — Fax (479) 709-9269 office@tkcmgt.com TURN KEY CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT June 7*, 2023 Board of Education Fort Smith Public Schools VIA EMAIL Re: Peak Innovation Center — Drainage Issues Dear Board Members, Turn Key Construction Management, Inc. (Turn Key) would like to go on record with our version of events in an attempt to aid the independent investigation the board requested during the school board meeting on 5/22/2023. In addition, we would like to address several comments which were made during the school board meeting which we feel like we did not have an opportunity to address. Finally, we would like to make comments to the Peak Innovation Center — Roof Drainage Systems Assessment for Fort Smith, Arkansas put together by HSA Engineering. 42” DRAIN PIPE ISSUE According to the letter written by Halff Engineering dated May 12, 2023, the flood on June 7*", 2022 was primarily caused by the plywood forms left in place inside the drainage structure. However, that same letter goes on to state “that the installation of the two (2) 42-inch pipes could be aggravating drainage at the site and recommended removing them as soon as possible.” Turn Key contests that the plywood forms were the primary cause of the flood event on June 7‘, 2022 due to the fact that according to the National Centers for Environmental information, the flood event on June 7*, 2022 was 1.04” more than the March 23", 2023 rain event. Considering how close the building came to flooding like the prior flood on March 23%, 2023, it seems like the primary cause of water backing up in the east lot has more to do with the size of the pipes instead of the fact that part of one pipe was partially blocked off during the first flood event. During the board meeting, the question of who recommended the 42” size pipes was asked several times and there was never a good answer given. You will see in the attached emails that Corgan and the District asked Halff to verify the sizing of the pipes before giving the final approval to move forward. It was Turn Key’s understanding that when we received the final design that this check had been completed by the design professionals and we were directed to move forward with the design. This point was previously made abundantly clear via a letter received from the Friday Law Firm on behalf of the Fort Smith Public Schools dated March 19", 2021. This letter states “The District agrees with your letter in so far as Turn Key, as contractor, does have an affirmative obligation to advise the District of any believed errors, inconsistencies, or omissions. This affirmative obligation exists prior to starting work, see for instance Sections 3.2.2 and 3.3.1 of AIA 201-2017, and during the progress of construction, see for instance Section 3.7.4 of AIA 201-2017. Turn Key has made its concerns clear. Nevertheless, the District, in consultation with the Corgan and Morrison-Shipley, has reached the informed conclusion that the current grading and drainage plan incorporated into the Contract Documents is sufficient. In light of that conclusion, Turn Key’s responsibilities are clear, construct the work in accordance with the Contract Documents.” Furthermore, Turn Key would like to note that in a letter to the Fort Smith Public Schools dated December 10", 2021 Turn Key acknowledged receipt of the change directive and was proceeding with the work. However, Turn Key also made note that we had been attempting to get a resolution to the drainage ditch since September 2", 2021 in the form of RFI #145 and every Owner, Architect, Contractor (OAC) meeting except one starting September 7, 2021. Had a clear directive been given in a timely manner, Turn Key would have had that work done long before the spring semester. ROOF DRAINAGE ASSESSMENT LETTER There are two major issues which Turn Key would like to address in the HSA Engineering report dated May 11°, 2023. First, there is a lot of discussion about the existing drainpipes located between the two buildings. It is noted in the letter that the existing pipes between the buildings are and have always been undersized for the amount of water which is coming off the roof in that location. Turn Key has no objection to that claim. What Turn Key would like to clarify is the scope of work pertaining to making sure the internal gutter system between the buildings is clearly defined. Please see the attached letters from Turn Key notifying the district of no warranty or guarantee on any roof patching or roof work done prior to the installation of the Coryell roof system. When the District elected to use Coryell roofing to provide a new roof on the building, it became the District’s and Coryell’s responsibility to ensure the roofing was adequately installed and that the transition from roof to gutter was properly installed. The failure of that area which caused the water to run down the fire wall became the responsibility of Coryell and the District when they elected to use a roofing contractor not under the scope of Turn Key. Second, there is discussion about the water intrusion coming up at the interface between the existing slab and the existing grade beam. The report goes on to note that “in addition to water, a significant amount of silt infiltrated the building”. Mainland Div. 3 Force Main – HDPE Force Majeure Dear Chris Stovall: Material deliveries for the 2016 SPLOST N. Mainland Division 3 Force Main project have been and continue to be negatively impacted by a resin shortage, caused by winter storms earlier this year. This catastrophic event led all HDPE manufacturers to declare force majeure between the project bid date and receipt of contract. This declaration voided the HDPE bid pricing, which was eventually replaced with a 38% cost increase. Below is a timeline of events dating back to the bid opening of this project: o o o o o o o 1/12/21 – Bid Date 2/15/21 – HDPE manufacturers began to declare Force Majeure, voiding bid pricing. 3/10/21 – Pre-construction meeting held at JWSC. o TBL has not received contract. (57 days post bid) o PVC needed to be ordered before 3/15/21 to hold bid pricing. Out of good faith, TBL used our Ferguson line of credit to order the PVC without a contract. o HDPE pricing was voided due to FM on 2/15/21. An updated HDPE quote would only be valid for 72 hours. TBL does not have line of credit capacity to procure this pipe without a contract, bond and NTO. o TBL informed JWSC that after the contract is received, a change order would be submitted for the increase in HDPE, as force majeure was out of TBL control. 3/18/21 – Ben Turnipseed signed the contract. 3/19/21 – JWSC sent contract via UPS 3/24/21 – TBL received contract and executed immediately. (71 days post bid) Requested updated HDPE pricing from Ferguson Waterworks. 3/29/21 –Received first HDPE price increase at 5PM. 38% at $168,800 – deadline 4/1. (After 4/1 is 54%)

excerpt: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) RFI # 1 DATE: SUBMITTED TO: Town of Golden Beach NEEDED BY: PROJECT: WELLNESS CENTER PROJECT SUBMITTED BY: John Bell Construction PROJECT #: RFP 2024-002 (Wellness Center) RFI DESCRIPTION 1. Please refer to the “Material Specifications” Excel Document in the Contract Documents. Please confirm an Allowance ($) for the Material Cost we are to carry in our Estimate for all the Material where “G.C.” is shown in the “MANF.” Column. 2. During the 01/23/2025 Pre-Bid Meeting, it was said that an Addendum would be released confirming that all Exterior Aluminum Paneling (Alucobond, etc.) is to be removed from the proposed Plan and replaced with Stucco and Paint. Please confirm. Also, please confirm the same is true for the FRP Panels. 3. Please confirm bidders are to provide a Bid Amount 100% PER PLAN, and a separate document showing Value Engineering/Alternate Cost Saving Options. We’d like to confirm we are not to include Value Engineered options in our Bid. 4. Please confirm the Bid Due Date can be extended. We’d like to explore as many Value Engineering and Cost Saving Options as possible, and this requires more time. ATTACHMENTS: RESPONSE TO RFI 1. The project budget has been allocated by the town. The recommended products were released in Addendum #2. There is no itemized allowance. 2. See updated drawings with Addendum #2 for ACM paneling changed to stucco. - The FRP panels remain in the design and are further detailed with recommended vendors. Please provide shop drawings as required. 3. Please do provide cost control options with comparisons. 4. The bid date has not been extended at this time. Town Manager and Town Clerk to confirm. RESPONSE BY: Eric Dempsey Architect, LLC DATE: 2025/01/31

reason: The document contains a formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
excerpt: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) RFI # 2 DATE: SUBMITTED TO: Town of Golden Beach NEEDED BY: PROJECT: WELLNESS CENTER PROJECT SUBMITTED BY: Pavion (AFAP) PROJECT #: RFP 2024-002 (Wellness Center) RFI DESCRIPTION I have attached a set of mark-up plans showing some of the changes that I would like to propose to the fire alarm system in order to cut down on cost. I would also propose that we use the same model of fire alarm panel that we have installed in the Civic building as it has a lower cost impact and is manufactured by the same company as the fire alarm panel in the specs for this project. We have also located a few items that will be required but were not accounted for in the initial fire alarm bid set of plans that will have a minor cost impact, however to prevent future change orders I feel it is best to address these issues upfront rather than as a change order later. Just running through the rough figures on this project I believe that the system as shown on the bid set of plans is probably about 25% higher in cost than is necessary due to the excess smoke detector coverage. ATTACHMENTS: RESPONSE TO RFI The sprinklers are to control the spread of fire and protect the facility, but the smoke detectors are meant to give occupants in the area of the fire an early warning, so they can evacuate the area before the fire prevents them from doing so, especially in an area with children. We have reviewed the code requirements and reduced the number of smoke detectors in line with the building code. See Addendum #2.
